# How to Use Z.ai to Compare Two Document Versions and Spot Every Change

> **In short:** You can upload an older and a newer version of a document to Z.ai and ask it to list the differences, then check each one against the originals. The key rule is to verify every change yourself, because the AI can miss small edits, especially in tables and scanned pages.

Comparing two versions of a contract, a school essay, a policy, or a report by eye is tiring, and it is easy to miss a changed number or a deleted sentence. In this guide you will learn a repeatable workflow: upload both files, ask for a structured list of changes, then use follow-up prompts to sort and check that list. It is written for people who already use Z.ai for everyday chats and want a more careful process.

## Before you start
- A Z.ai account and a chat you can open in your web browser or the Z.ai app. You already know how to start a chat and send a message, so we skip that part.
- Two versions of the same document saved as files on your computer or phone, such as Word files, PDFs, or plain text. Name them something clear like "report-v1-march" and "report-v2-april".
- Some features, file types, and file sizes can depend on your plan and on what Z.ai currently supports. If an upload fails, check the current help information on Z.ai's official website.
- Plan about 20 to 30 minutes for your first comparison.

## Step 1 — Check that both files are readable
Before uploading anything, open each file and make sure you can select and read the text. Scroll through both versions quickly. This matters because a scanned page is often just a picture of text, and the AI may read it less accurately than typed text.

If a file is a scan or a photo, look for a way to save it as a text-based PDF or Word document from your scanner or printing app. If the file is already typed, you are ready to go.

💬 Example: Before uploading, I'll check that I can highlight words in "report-v1-march" and "report-v2-april".

You'll know it worked when you can select words in both files and they look like normal typed text.

## Step 2 — Upload the older version first
Open a new chat in Z.ai. Look for an attachment button near the message box, often shown as a paperclip or a plus sign. Tap or click it, choose the older version of your document, and wait until the file name appears above or beside your message box.

If you don't see a paperclip or plus sign, look for an upload or "add file" option in the message area or in a menu near it. Availability can differ by device and plan, so if you truly can't find an upload option, the document may need to be pasted as text instead. Copy the full text from the file and paste it into the message box.

💬 Example: Attach "report-v1-march" and send the message "This is the original version. Please wait for the second file before you comment."

You'll know it worked when the file name shows up in the chat and Z.ai acknowledges the file, usually with a short reply confirming it received your message.

## Step 3 — Upload the newer version and label the roles
Now attach the newer version in the same chat. The label matters: the AI needs to know which file is the baseline and which is the update, or it may describe changes backward. Send a message that names each file clearly so there is no confusion later.

Keep the message simple. Write one sentence for each file, and say that you will ask for the comparison in the next message. This gives you a checkpoint before the real work starts.

💬 Example: Attach "report-v2-april" and send the message "This is the updated version. Treat the March file as the original and the April file as the new one."

You'll know it worked when Z.ai's reply repeats which file is the original and which is the new one, in its own words. If it gets the order wrong, correct it before continuing.

## Step 4 — Ask for a structured list of changes
Now ask for the comparison, and be specific about the format. A vague request like "what's different?" often produces a loose summary that misses small edits. A structured request gives you a checklist you can verify.

Ask the AI to sort changes into categories such as added text, removed text, changed numbers or dates, and changed names. Ask it to quote the short original wording for each change. Quoting gives you something concrete to check against the file.

💬 Example: "Compare the original and new versions. List every change under four headings: added text, removed text, changed numbers or dates, and changed names. For each change, give the original wording and the new wording, and state the section where it appears."

You'll know it worked when you see a list organized under those headings, with original and new wording side by side. If the answer is only a short summary, reply: "Please list every change individually, not a summary."

## Step 5 — Verify each change against the originals
This is the most important step, and it is the one most people skip. Take the list Z.ai gave you and check each item against the two files, one at a time. Use the search function in your document app if you have one, and search for the exact quoted wording. If the wording is not found in the file, the AI made an error.

Mark each item as confirmed, incorrect, or missed. Missed changes are the ones you find yourself while reading the files. Keep a short list of them, because you will use it in the next step.

💬 Example: "You listed the budget change from 12,000 to 14,500. I searched both files and cannot find 12,000 in the original. Please show me the exact sentence where it appears."

You'll know it worked when you have a short list of confirmed changes and a separate list of anything the AI got wrong or missed.

## Step 6 — Ask a follow-up to sort and fix the list
Now build on the earlier answer. Give Z.ai your confirmed changes and the missed items, and ask it to rank them by importance and to draft a short summary you could share with someone else. Because it already knows the documents from this chat, you don't need to re-upload anything.

Read the final summary carefully before you share it. The AI may phrase a change more strongly than the document does, so make sure each sentence matches what you verified.

💬 Example: "Here are the changes I confirmed and two I found myself: [paste your confirmed list here]. Sort them from most to least important, and write a five-sentence summary I can send to my team."

You'll know it worked when you get a ranked list and a short summary, and every item matches a change you verified in Step 5.

## Common mistakes
- **Trusting the summary without checking it.** The AI can miss a single changed digit or a deleted clause. The fix is Step 5: search for every quoted line in the original files before you rely on the list.
- **Uploading scanned or blurry pages.** Text from a poor-quality image may be read incorrectly, so changes can look fake or disappear. The fix is Step 1: convert scans to text-based files first, or type out the important sections yourself.
- **Mixing up which file is older.** If the order is wrong, every "added" line becomes "removed". The fix is Step 3: name each file clearly and check that Z.ai repeats the order correctly before you ask for the comparison.

One honest limit: Z.ai can help you find and organize differences, but it cannot guarantee it caught every one, and it cannot decide what a change means legally, financially, or medically. For a contract or an official form, use your own careful reading and ask a qualified professional for advice on what the changes mean for you.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Comparing a lease renewal, a school permission form, or a club's updated rules against the old version becomes a quick checklist instead of a long read-through, as long as you verify each item.
- **For your business or work:** Teams can compare draft reports, policy updates, or meeting notes from one week to the next, then send the verified list to colleagues instead of the full documents.
- **If you want to go further:** Try asking Z.ai to compare three versions in sequence, and then ask it to explain how the wording changed over time. Always keep the verification step, and check each claim against the originals before you act on it.

## Try it now
Pick any two versions of a short document you already have, such as two drafts of a note or a list you edited. Upload the older one, then the newer one, and ask Z.ai for a list of changes under the four headings from Step 4. Then search for three items in the original files to see how well the list matches.
